chapter: Wynn: New York and Chicago bands
title: Return to New York and the union card problem
summary: Wynn returned to New York, played at Small's breakfast dances, angered the union delegate Minton, and could not take a regular job.

story.theme_name: The musicians' union: cards, locals, and the Black-white merger
story.community_name: The musicians' union: cards, scale and the black-white merger

blocks.x: We were talking about the Savoy...

Yeah, they were working at the Savoy then. So I just got in town, well, actually, they're the first ones that knew I was back and whatnot. They told me their program, and they were working up there and everything. So they say, I never belonged to the New York local, you know. In fact, at that time, I was under the impression I didn't belong to any local because I hadn't paid any dues in Chicago for a period of five years, four or five years. So they say, well, we've got to arrange it, we've got to smuggle you in here, and one of those things. So they were having the breakfast dances at Small's. So I went there and I ran into a lot of the Chicago musicians at the Newman. It was strictly professional breakfast dances, you know. And everybody, here's old Al, come on and play. So I get up to play, and I get up and blow some with them. I'm so happy and so thrilled to be back. And as it would happen, the Union man was in there, which was... Minton was there at that time. Minton was there, Minton. And it was near election. He and Peekaboo Jimmy was running against Minton, see. And so they heard me. And Tom and Bashe come and say, that's the worst thing you could have ever done. And they go, well I'm just glad to be back home and out having fun and seeing the boys and anxious to play because I mean the only things that I'd heard from over here was the canned music, you know. So it was a natural mistake. So that sort of cramped things with the Union. Come to find out, I couldn't, I rode out here. I had all kind of jobs in New York. But I went to the Cotton Club with Cal. Fletcher warned me. But my heart was set on going with Bashe and Tommy. In fact, we would have rehearsals every day and those rehearsals were so much in job. And we would sit up there and rehearse all day long, you know, and drink root beer. There was a root beer place. You could get a gallon of root beer for about fifteen cents. And it was just fascinating. But due to the fact that Peekaboo Jimmy was running against Minton for his job, Peekaboo couldn't give me the pass to do anything. I mean Minton couldn't because Peekaboo would tell, would go downtown and tell everything. And so it sums down. So I tried to join outright to say, well, first you got to get a release from Chicago. I write that, yeah.
